intro:
A Private Limited Company is more than just a business registration.

It gives your business a separate legal identity, structured ownership and a strong foundation for funding, team building and future expansion.

Whether you are starting a new business, building a startup or planning to scale an existing venture, choosing the right structure from the beginning can make future growth much easier.

Start Right → Build Credibility → Raise Capital → Expand
what_is_service:
A Private Limited Company is a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013.

It has a legal identity separate from its shareholders and operates through a structured ownership and management framework involving shareholders and directors.

It is one of the most suitable structures for entrepreneurs who want to build a scalable, professionally managed and investment-ready business.
who_should_choose:
A Private Limited Company can be suitable for:

Startups

Two or more founders

Growing businesses

Technology companies

E-commerce businesses

Manufacturing businesses

Businesses planning to raise investment

Businesses planning ESOPs

Companies dealing with corporates and institutions

Entrepreneurs planning long-term expansion

If your vision is to build something bigger than a small owner-managed business, a Private Limited Company can provide the structure required for that journey.
key_benefits:
Separate Legal Identity

The company has its own legal identity separate from its shareholders.

Limited Liability

Shareholders generally have limited liability, subject to applicable law and circumstances such as personal guarantees.

Structured Ownership

Ownership is represented through shares, making founder and investor ownership easier to define.

Funding Friendly

A Private Limited Company is generally the preferred structure for angel investors, venture capital and equity investment.

ESOP Opportunity

Eligible companies can create ESOP structures to attract and retain employees, subject to applicable law.

Perpetual Succession

The company continues to exist despite changes in shareholders or directors.

Professional Business Structure

A corporate structure can improve the way the business presents itself to customers, vendors, employees, lenders and investors.
eligibility:
Generally, a Private Limited Company requires:

Minimum 2 Shareholders

Minimum 2 Directors

At least 1 Resident Director, as required under applicable law

Registered Office in India

Unique and acceptable company name

Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)

Lawful business activity

Proposed share capital and shareholding structure

There is no prescribed minimum paid-up capital requirement for a normal Private Limited Company.

faqs.question: How many people are required to start a Private Limited Company?
faqs.answer: Generally, a minimum of two members/shareholders and two directors are required. The same individuals can act as both shareholders and directors, subject to applicable law.

faqs.question: Is there any minimum capital requirement?
faqs.answer: There is no prescribed minimum paid-up capital requirement for incorporating a normal Private Limited Company.

faqs.question: Can I register a company from anywhere in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MCA incorporation process is largely digital, although the company must have a registered office in India and comply with applicable requirements.

faqs.question: How long does company registration take?
faqs.answer: We generally estimate approximately 10 working days, subject to name approval, documents, MCA processing and any resubmission.

faqs.question: Is a Private Limited Company better than an LLP?
faqs.answer: It depends on your plans. A Private Limited Company is generally more suitable for equity funding, multiple shareholders and scalable startup structures, whereas an LLP can be suitable for partner-driven professional and service businesses.

faqs.question: Can a Private Limited Company raise investment?
faqs.answer: Yes. Subject to applicable laws and procedures, a Private Limited Company can issue shares and raise equity capital from eligible investors.

faqs.question: Can a Private Limited Company give ESOPs?
faqs.answer: Yes, ESOPs can be structured subject to the Companies Act and other applicable requirements.

faqs.question: Is audit compulsory for a Private Limited Company?
faqs.answer: A company is generally required to have its financial statements audited under the Companies Act, irrespective of whether it has significant turnover or profit.

faqs.question: Is GST automatically included with company registration?
faqs.answer: No. GST registration is separate and its requirement depends on the nature of business, turnover and other applicable GST provisions.

faqs.question: Can The Corporate Hub handle compliance after registration?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can assist with applicable accounting, GST, income tax, ROC, payroll and other business compliance requirements.

intro:
Want to start a business with partners but don't necessarily need the share-based structure of a Private Limited Company?

A Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) combines the flexibility of a partnership with a separate legal identity and limited liability structure.

It can be particularly suitable for consultants, professionals, agencies, service businesses and closely held businesses where the founders want to operate and grow together as partners.

Partners → Professional Structure → Flexible Management → Growth
what_is_service:
A Limited Liability Partnership is a separate legal entity registered under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.

Instead of shareholders and directors, an LLP operates through Partners and Designated Partners.

The rights, responsibilities, contribution, profit-sharing and management arrangement between partners are primarily structured through the LLP Agreement, subject to applicable law.
who_should_choose:
An LLP can be suitable for:

Consultants & advisory businesses

Professional service firms

IT & technology service providers

Digital & creative agencies

Architects and designers

Family or closely held businesses

Two or more entrepreneurs starting together

Businesses where partners actively manage operations

Businesses not presently focused on raising conventional equity investment

For regulated professions, the applicable professional laws and regulations should also be considered before selecting the entity structure.
key_benefits:
Separate Legal Identity

The LLP has a legal identity separate from its partners.

Limited Liability

Partners generally enjoy limited liability, subject to the LLP Act and exceptions such as fraud, wrongful acts and personal guarantees.

Flexible Partnership Structure

The LLP Agreement can define:

Contribution | Profit Sharing | Remuneration | Responsibilities | Decision-Making | Admission & Retirement of Partners

No Conventional Share Capital

An LLP works through partner contributions and partnership rights rather than company share capital.

Perpetual Succession

The LLP can continue despite changes in its partners, subject to applicable law.

Comparatively Flexible Management

An LLP generally has a simpler internal governance framework than a Private Limited Company.
eligibility:
Generally, LLP registration requires:

Minimum 2 Partners

Minimum 2 Designated Partners

At least 1 Designated Partner resident in India, as required under applicable law

Registered Office in India

Unique and acceptable LLP name

Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)

Lawful business activity

Agreed capital contribution

Agreed profit-sharing ratio

There is generally no prescribed minimum capital contribution for forming an LLP.

tax_compliance:
An LLP is generally taxed as a partnership firm under the Income-tax Act.

Income Tax Rate

30% + applicable surcharge + 4% Health & Education Cess

Other provisions, including Alternate Minimum Tax (AMT), may apply depending upon the LLP's circumstances.

TDS on Payments to Partners – Section 194T

From 1 April 2025, Section 194T provides for TDS at 10% on specified payments such as salary, remuneration, commission, bonus or interest made/credited by a firm/LLP to a partner where the prescribed threshold and conditions are satisfied.

Ongoing Compliance

Depending upon applicability, an LLP may need:

Accounting | Income Tax Return | LLP Annual Return | Statement of Account & Solvency | GST | TDS | Partner TDS | Audit | Other Business-Specific Compliance

Partners can structure their contribution and economic rights through the LLP Agreement, allowing founders to build the business through a partnership model.

Add Partners as You Expand

This can help bring in:

2 Partners → Team → Clients → New Partners → Multiple Locations

An LLP can provide a formal structure without necessarily requiring the complete shareholder and board framework of a company.

faqs.question: What is the minimum number of partners required for an LLP?
faqs.answer: An LLP requires a minimum of two partners and at least two designated partners.

faqs.question: Is there any minimum capital required?
faqs.answer: There is generally no prescribed minimum capital contribution for incorporating an LLP.

faqs.question: Is an LLP a separate legal entity?
faqs.answer: Yes. An LLP has a separate legal identity from its partners.

faqs.question: Is LLP better than a Private Limited Company?
faqs.answer: Neither structure is universally better. An LLP can be more suitable for partner-driven professional and service businesses, while a Private Limited Company is generally better suited for businesses planning equity investment, ESOPs and wider share ownership.

faqs.question: Can an LLP raise investment?
faqs.answer: Partners can introduce capital and new partners may be admitted subject to applicable law and the LLP Agreement. However, an LLP does not issue equity shares like a Private Limited Company, making it less suitable for conventional VC/angel equity funding.

faqs.question: How are profits shared in an LLP?
faqs.answer: Profit-sharing arrangements are generally specified in the LLP Agreement.

faqs.question: Can partners take remuneration from an LLP?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to the LLP Agreement and applicable provisions of the Income-tax Act. Tax deductibility and TDS implications should be evaluated separately.

faqs.question: Is audit compulsory for every LLP?
faqs.answer: No. Statutory audit requirements for an LLP depend upon prescribed thresholds and applicable law.

faqs.question: Can an LLP be registered from anywhere in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. The registration process is largely digital, provided the LLP has a registered office in India and fulfils applicable requirements.

faqs.question: Can The Corporate Hub handle LLP compliance after registration?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can assist with LLP filings, accounting, GST, income tax, TDS and other applicable business compliances.

intro:
Want to own 100% of your business but still operate through a structured company?

A One Person Company (OPC) allows a single entrepreneur to start a company with one member/shareholder, while creating a legal identity separate from the individual owner.

It can be an ideal step for entrepreneurs who have outgrown the idea of a simple proprietorship but are not yet ready to bring in another shareholder.

One Founder → One Company → Professional Identity → Future Growth
what_is_service:
A One Person Company (OPC) is a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 with only one member/shareholder.

Unlike a proprietorship, an OPC has a separate legal identity from its owner.

The OPC can have its own:

PAN | Bank Account | Assets | Contracts | Applicable Business Registrations & Licences

This creates a clearer distinction between:

You as an Individual

and

Your Business as a Company
who_should_choose:
An OPC can be suitable for:

Solo entrepreneurs

Individual consultants

Online & e-commerce entrepreneurs

Small manufacturers

Individual service providers

Business owners moving from proprietorship

Founders who want 100% ownership initially

Entrepreneurs planning to build a corporate identity

Solo founders who may convert into a Private Limited Company as they expand

It is particularly useful when you want to start alone today but keep the possibility of a larger company tomorrow.
key_benefits:
100% Single-Member Ownership

You can start the company without bringing in another shareholder merely for the purpose of having a second owner.

Separate Legal Identity

The OPC is legally separate from its member.

Separate PAN

Unlike a proprietorship, where the proprietor's PAN is used for income-tax purposes, an OPC receives its own PAN as a company.

Limited Liability

The member generally enjoys limited liability, subject to applicable law, fraud, personal guarantees and other exceptions.

Corporate Identity

Operate through a registered company structure while dealing with customers, vendors, banks and institutions.

Perpetual Succession

The nominee mechanism provides continuity in prescribed circumstances.

Future Conversion

As your ownership requirements change, an OPC can be converted into another form of company, including a Private Limited Company, in accordance with applicable law.

Minimum 1 Director

1 Nominee

Registered Office in India

Unique and acceptable company name

Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)

Lawful business activity

Proposed share capital

The eligibility of the member and nominee is subject to the applicable Companies Act and Rules.

There is no prescribed minimum paid-up capital requirement for a normal OPC.

faqs.question: Can one person start a company in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. An eligible individual can incorporate an OPC subject to the requirements of the Companies Act and applicable Rules.

faqs.question: Is OPC different from a proprietorship?
faqs.answer: Yes. A proprietorship does not create a separate legal person from the proprietor. An OPC is a separate company incorporated under the Companies Act.

faqs.question: Does an OPC get a separate PAN?
faqs.answer: Yes. An OPC receives a PAN in the company's name, whereas a proprietorship generally uses the proprietor's PAN for income-tax purposes.

faqs.question: Can licences be obtained in the OPC's name?
faqs.answer:
Applicable registrations and licences such as GST, FSSAI, IEC and other business-specific registrations may be obtained in the company's name where the relevant law permits or requires them.

The type of licence—for example, Basic, State or Central FSSAI—depends upon the applicable eligibility criteria and not merely on being an OPC.

faqs.question: Is a nominee compulsory for an OPC?
faqs.answer: Yes. A nominee is required as part of the OPC framework, subject to applicable provisions.

faqs.question: Can an OPC have employees?
faqs.answer: Yes. Having only one member does not mean the company can have only one person working in the business. An OPC can employ people subject to applicable labour and other laws.

faqs.question: Can an OPC raise investment?
faqs.answer: An OPC is built around a single-member structure. If additional equity shareholders or conventional equity investment are required, conversion into an appropriate company structure may be necessary.

faqs.question: Can an OPC be converted into a Private Limited Company?
faqs.answer: Yes, conversion is possible in accordance with the Companies Act and applicable Rules.

faqs.question: Is statutory audit compulsory for an OPC?
faqs.answer: As a company, an OPC is generally required to have its financial statements audited under the Companies Act, subject to applicable provisions.

faqs.question: Should I choose OPC or proprietorship?
faqs.answer: Choose based on your business size, risk, taxation, compliance requirements and future growth plan. Proprietorship offers simplicity, while OPC provides a separate corporate identity and limited liability structure.

intro:
If you want to start an NGO for charitable, educational, social, environmental, healthcare, research or community-focused activities, a Section 8 Company can provide a highly structured non-profit framework.

Unlike a simple trust structure, a Section 8 Company operates under the Companies Act, 2013, with defined governance through members, directors and MCA compliance.

It is suitable for organisations that want to build:

Credibility → Governance → Donations → CSR Opportunities → Long-Term Impact
what_is_service:
A Section 8 Company is a non-profit company incorporated under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013.

It is formed for objects such as:

Education | Charity | Social Welfare | Research | Environment | Healthcare | Sports | Art | Science | Community Development

Its profits or income are applied towards its stated objectives rather than being distributed as dividend to members.

A Section 8 Company combines:

Non-Profit Purpose + Corporate Structure

Structured Governance

The organisation operates through:

Members | Directors | Memorandum | Articles | Statutory Records

Professional NGO Structure

A Section 8 Company provides a formal corporate framework that can be useful when dealing with:

Corporates | Donors | Institutions | Government Bodies | Grant Agencies

12A / 12AB Eligibility

An eligible Section 8 Company can separately apply for income-tax registration commonly referred to as 12A / 12AB.

80G Eligibility

CSR Opportunity

An eligible Section 8 Company can act as a CSR implementing agency subject to the applicable CSR Rules and required registrations. MCA's CSR guidance confirms that Section 8 companies can be eligible implementing agencies, with 12A and 80G generally required for non-government entities and CSR-1 registration also relevant.

Long-Term Continuity

The organisation can continue despite changes in members or directors, subject to applicable law.

No distribution of dividend to members

The proposed objects and activities should clearly support the organisation's non-profit purpose.

faqs.question: What is a Section 8 Company?
faqs.answer: It is a non-profit company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 for charitable or socially beneficial objectives.

faqs.question: Can a Section 8 Company make profit?
faqs.answer: It may generate income or surplus, but the profits are required to be applied towards its stated objects and cannot be distributed as dividend to members.

faqs.question: Is 12A / 12AB automatic with Section 8 registration?
faqs.answer: No. It requires a separate application and approval under the Income-tax framework.

faqs.question: Is 80G automatically available?
faqs.answer: No. 80G is a separate approval and is subject to eligibility and applicable conditions.

faqs.question: Can a Section 8 Company receive CSR funds?
faqs.answer: It can be eligible to act as a CSR implementing agency subject to the Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, required registrations and other applicable conditions.

faqs.question: Is Section 8 better than a Trust?
faqs.answer: Not always. Section 8 offers a structured corporate framework, while a trust can be simpler and more appropriate for certain charitable activities.

faqs.question: Can a Section 8 Company receive foreign donations?
faqs.answer: Only subject to applicable FCRA registration or prior permission and related compliance. Section 8 registration alone does not permit unrestricted foreign contributions.

faqs.question: How long does registration take?
faqs.answer: We generally estimate approximately 20 working days, subject to MCA processing and document readiness.

faqs.question: Can a Section 8 Company operate across India?
faqs.answer: Yes. Subject to its objects, licences and applicable laws, it can undertake activities across India.

faqs.question: Can The Corporate Hub handle compliance after incorporation?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can assist with 12A / 12AB, 80G, CSR-1, accounting, taxation, ROC compliance and NGO-related advisory.

faqs.question: Is every new company eligible for Startup India?
faqs.answer: No. Merely being newly incorporated is not enough. The business must satisfy the applicable DPIIT eligibility criteria, including innovation/improvement or the prescribed scalable-business criteria.

faqs.question: What is the current turnover limit?
faqs.answer: Under the 2026 framework, the turnover threshold is below ₹200 crore for normal recognised startups and below ₹300 crore for qualifying DeepTech startups.

faqs.question: How old can a startup be?
faqs.answer: Generally, a normal startup can remain recognised for up to 10 years, while qualifying DeepTech startups can have an extended period of up to 20 years, subject to applicable conditions.

faqs.question: Does Startup India give 3 years of tax exemption automatically?
faqs.answer: No. DPIIT recognition itself does not provide automatic income-tax exemption. Eligible startups need to separately satisfy and apply under Section 80-IAC.

faqs.question: Does DPIIT give funding after registration?
faqs.answer: No. DPIIT recognition does not guarantee a loan, grant or investment.

faqs.question: Can an LLP obtain Startup India Recognition?
faqs.answer: Yes, an eligible LLP can apply for DPIIT recognition.

faqs.question: Can a proprietorship obtain DPIIT Startup Recognition?
faqs.answer: A sole proprietorship is not included among the eligible entity structures listed under the current DPIIT recognition criteria.

faqs.question: Is Startup India useful for an existing business?
faqs.answer: Potentially yes, provided the entity remains within the prescribed age, turnover and other eligibility criteria and satisfies the innovation/scalability requirements.

faqs.question: Is Startup India registration available across India?
faqs.answer: Yes. DPIIT Startup Recognition is a Central Government framework and is not restricted to Gujarat.

faqs.question: Is the DPIIT certificate itself chargeable by the Government?
faqs.answer: The Startup India portal states that the Ministry does not charge a fee for DPIIT Certificate of Recognition or Certificate of Eligibility. Professional advisory/support charges, where separately engaged, are different from a government recognition fee.
